title: FTSE Russell US indexes — June semi-annual reconstitution, implemented after the close
source: EST: rule-derived from the index owner's own ground rules; no 2027-dated calendar published yet. FTSE Russell, "Russell US Equity Indexes" construction and methodology, v7.2, August 2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research from lseg.com/content/dam/ftse-russell/en_us/documents/ground-rules/russell-us-indexes-construction-and-methodology.pdf (HTTP 200, 746,491 bytes, 50 pages) and text-extracted in-session by inflating the PDF's content streams -- not inherited from the sibling that proposed this id. TWO independent clauses of that document give the date, and this session proved they never disagree. (1) Section 4.2.3, verbatim: "Reconstitution occurs on the fourth Friday in June and the second Friday in December." Appendix F's schedule table repeats it as Implementation = "4th Friday of June", and defines it: "Implementation is the day changes are made after the close of the market and become effective at the open on the Monday following." June 2027's Fridays are 06-04 / 06-11 / 06-18 / 06-25, so the fourth is 2027-06-25, effective at the open Monday 2027-06-28. (2) Section 9.3.1 states a CARVE-OUT the proposing sibling did not read: the quarterly review implements on the "fourth Friday in June (unless the last Friday occurs on the 29th or 30th, when reconstitution will occur on the Friday prior)". Enumerated mechanically this session for every June 2005-2040, the two readings agree in 36 of 36 years and disagree in 0 -- a June with a 29th/30th last Friday is exactly a June with five Fridays, whose Friday-prior IS its fourth. So 2027-06-25 does not depend on which clause is read, and the carve-out is a no-op restatement rather than a risk. CORROBORATED by the owner's own reconstitution page (lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/russell-reconstitution, HTTP 200, 228,333 bytes, 13,681 characters of extracted text this session against the 838 a sibling got on the same day), whose FAQ states "changes to the Russell Indexes are implemented after the close of US markets on the fourth Friday in June" and dates the two instances the rule has already produced -- June 2026 = "June 26, 2026" and December 2026 = "December 11, 2026" -- both of which the fourth-Friday / second-Friday rule reproduces exactly. 2027-06-25 is a full NYSE session; the only June 2027 closure is Friday 06-18 (Juneteenth observed). Rank Day is the last business day of April = Friday 2027-04-30, and preliminary lists publish five weeks before implementation = Friday 2027-05-21 (the five-week convention confirmed against BOTH published instances: 2026-05-22 to 2026-06-26 is exactly 35 days, and December's four-week convention gives exactly 28 from 2026-11-13 to 2026-12-11). Filed estimate, not confirmed, for two reasons stated plainly: no FTSE Russell 2027 reconstitution calendar exists yet (the ground rules say one "is published each spring", so the 2027 calendar is not due until spring 2027 -- this is not a blocked fetch, it is an unpublished document), and this calendar's source-prefix vocabulary has no confirmed-tier member for an index owner (IR:/BLS:/FED:/SEC:/OCC:/TSY:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:/PJM:/CAL:), so even an owner-published date could not be labelled honestly today. Promote on a published FTSE Russell 2027 recon calendar naming 2027-06-25, once a prefix exists for it. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-06), which found the id existed only as proposals/russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25.from-sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-06-30.json; that proposal was read in full first and its findings are carried forward, not discarded. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE INHERITED FRAMING, both from the owner's own primaries. (1) TITLE: the proposal called this "the annual June reconstitution". It is not annual any more -- ground rules v7.2 section 4.2.3 states reconstitution occurs in June AND December, and the owner's page says "Beginning in 2026, the Russell Indexes are reconstituted semi-annually". 2026 is the first year of the new regime and June 2026 was its first June leg. (2) THE SECOND LEG WAS UNTRACKED: the first December reconstitution in the index family's history implements after the close on 2026-12-11 -- 96 days out, not 292 -- and lands on the same session as two `high` entries this calendar already carries (cr-expiry-2026-12-11, government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11), one day after cpi-2026-12-10 and two after fomc-2026-12-09. Proposed this session as proposals/russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11.from-<this-id>.json, together with the June 2027 preliminary-list date (2027-05-21). WHAT THIS SESSION MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED, and it is mostly negative: the proposing sibling flagged "reliably the year's heaviest US closing auction" as received wisdom it had not measured. Measured on IWM and SPY daily bars 2006-2026 (Yahoo, fetched this session), the recon session is the year's #1 IWM volume day in 0 of 21 years (best rank 7th, in 2016 -- which is the Brexit referendum result day, not a recon effect), is June's own heaviest IWM session in 2 of 21, and out-volumes June's own quad-witching in 10 of 20 -- a coin flip. Its median whole-day volume ratio is 1.42x trailing-60d (1.33x excluding Brexit). That refutes a LOOSE reading only: the owner's own figure for June 2026 is $219.9bn (NYSE) + $334.0bn (Nasdaq) traded "in the closing moments", an AUCTION measure that whole-day ETF volume cannot see, and this session had no auction-level instrument. The index-effect shape (small-caps outperform into the print, reverse after) IS visible -- IWM-vs-SPY D0->D+5 mean -0.87% against -0.06% unconditional, one-sided bootstrap p=4.8%, n=11 -- but it does NOT survive its own placebo: the same test on the fourth Friday of all twelve months puts June at the extreme yet flags one month at p<0.05, which is what chance alone produces from twelve tries (Sidak-corrected ~44%), and p swings 1.7% to 24.4% on window length alone. So it is a registered hypothesis, not an edge -- and its reversal leg would require shorting, blocked house-wide (trade-playbooks.md, "No shorting in the first cut"). No house playbook is index-flow- or calendar-keyed (trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-grepped 2026-09-06 for rebalanc|index effect|select sector|capping|secondary reweight|reconstitution|russell, zero hits), so this entry widens caution and licenses nothing. Impact medium, unchanged from the proposal: market-wide and mechanically forced, but with a measured null on the one path that could have made it actionable. `symbols` stays empty, matching every other market-structure entry here -- IWM was this session's measurement instrument, not a house name. Kind `sector` matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane.
